title: The Hollow Tithe
blurb: A toll road, a levy counted in timber, and a warden who stopped writing home.

brief.premise: a forest toll road where the levy is counted in felled timber
brief.storyline: the player is looking for a sibling who took the warden's badge and stopped writing
brief.tone: damp, wry, and short of daylight
brief.protagonist: a timber-tallier walking the road out of season

lore.title: The Hollow Tithe
lore.premise: The crown stopped asking for coin three winters ago and started asking for timber. The forest has been paying ever since, and the road that carries it is the only law out here.
lore.era: the third winter of the timber levy
lore.tone: damp, wry, and short of daylight

467299905.name: Shoulder Bottoms
467299905.blurb: Shoulder Bottoms is highland country, and keeps to itself.
ambient: The wind moves across the highland.
Somewhere off the track, an axe stops mid-stroke.
A cart has been through here recently, and heavily.
Sap has stuck your sleeve to your arm again.
The stumps beside the road are fresh, and numbered in white paint.

2259585032.name: The Warden's Shoulder
2259585032.blurb: High open ground where the road climbs out of the trees and the crown can finally see it.
2259585032.culture: Wardens, weighers and people who have learned to be elsewhere.
lore: Every cart is weighed twice on the Shoulder, and the second weight is the one that counts.
ambient: The wind up here has nothing to break it.
You can see the road for a mile in both directions, which is the point.

4222914290.name: The Long Fell
4222914290.blurb: Deep forest cut by one road and a hundred arguments about who owns the trees beside it.
4222914290.culture: Fellers and cart-drivers who count in cords and trust in writing.
lore: A cord of oak buys more here than a purse of silver.
The Compact keeps its own tally, and it does not match the crown's.
ambient: The canopy closes over the road and the light goes green.
Somewhere off the track, an axe stops mid-stroke.
Sap has stuck your sleeve to your arm again.

npcs.name: Ilse Marrow
npcs.appearance: Broad, wind-burnt, two fingers short on her left hand and unbothered about it.

arc.title: The Hollow Tithe
arc.premise: Your sister took the warden's badge, walked the road east, and stopped writing. The tally she was keeping stopped adding up at about the same time.

quest.name: Take the tally to Stonewait
quest.description: Ilse's own count is short by a cord a month. The weighing station up the high road is where the crown's number is made. Carry it there and find the warden at the gate.

beats.journal: Ilse Marrow says a warden came through in autumn with a new badge and no name, and that the Cord House tally has been short ever since.

quest.name: Ask Ott Pell about the true weight
quest.description: Cull signs two tallies and only one is honest. Ott Pell keeps the honest one, and does not keep it here. He is on the bench inside the walls.

beats.journal: Warden Cull confirms it: the badge was signed out in autumn and never signed back in. Two tallies leave Stonewait, and only one of them is true.

quest.name: Follow the ledger to Harrowmere
quest.description: Ott sold his true count to Factor Odell, in Harrowmere, where the timber stops being timber and starts being money. The road runs on east. Go and read it.

beats.journal: Ott Pell keeps the honest weights nowhere near the station. He sold the lot down the road to a factor in Harrowmere who buys paper and does not ask where it came from.
Factor Odell bought a full ledger from a warden in autumn, at four parts in five, and was asked to forget her. He remembers the hand it was written in. So do you.

ending.title: The hand you know
ending.subtitle: read in the back room of Odell's, by one lamp

sections.heading: The ledger
sections.body: It is not the crown's book and it was never meant to be. Two columns to a page: what the road carried, and what the yard received. The second is always the larger, and the difference is always about a cord, and it has been about a cord every month since the levy doubled.

sections.heading: The hand
sections.body: Small, hard, and slanted to the left, the way she wrote everything from the time she was nine. She kept the true count for three winters, sold it to a man who buys paper and does not ask, and asked him to forget her. She did not stop writing. She stopped writing to you.

sections.heading: And now
sections.body: You know where she went and why she stopped writing, and you are holding the reason in both hands. Nobody is waiting on you. The road out of Harrowmere runs west, back the way you came, and the levy will be counted again next month whatever you do about it.

hello.speech: Out of season and on foot. You are either lost or you are looking for somebody.

choices.text: Looking for a warden. New badge, autumn.
What is wrong with the tally here?

warden.speech: She came through, yes. Would not give a name, which around here is the same as giving one. Went up the high road toward Stonewait — that is the weighing station, north and uphill, you cannot miss it — and did not come back down.

choices.text: That is enough to go on.

tally.speech: Short. Every month since the levy doubled, and always by about a cord. I keep my own count because I am not a fool. Here — take a copy up the road and see whose face changes.

actions.description: Ilse's own count, in a small hard hand, folded twice.

hello-after.speech: You still have my count, I see. Good. It is worth more out of this house than in it.

again.speech: Back again. There is stew, and there is the other stew.

hello.speech: The road is open and the weighbridge is not. State your business or use the verge.

choices.text: I am looking for a warden.

hello-tally.speech: You are carrying paper. I can always tell. Whose is it?

badge.speech: Signed out in autumn. Never signed back in. I have written it up four times and four times it has come back initialled and unread.

weights.speech: Two tallies leave this station. One goes to the crown and one is true. I sign both, which is the part I would rather you did not write down.

east.speech: Ott keeps the honest weight and Ott does not keep it here. Ask him, not me — he is on the bench inside the wall, doing sums I cannot bear to watch.

choices.text: The bench inside the wall. I will find him.

again.speech: Still here. Still open. Still not the weighbridge.

hello.speech: Paper, timber, or trouble? I buy the first, weigh the second, and price the third rather high.

choices.text: A ledger, sold to you in autumn.
Why does the Crown Yard take more cord than the road carries?

ledger.speech: A warden, yes. Four parts in five, which was generous, and she asked to be forgotten, which was cheap. I have an excellent memory and a very short one, depending.

yard.speech: Because the road is not the only way in, and the yard is not the only one counting. You did not need me to tell you that. You needed somebody to say it out loud.

price.speech: On whether the person asking is family. You have her hand about the mouth, if not the sense. It is in the back room, under the counter, and it is not for sale twice. Read it there and then decide what you are going to do about it.

choices.text: Then I will read it here.

again.speech: Back. The ledger has not moved and neither have I.
